title: Hubble image of PGC 6240
caption: The elliptical galaxy PGC 6240, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: PGC 6240 · constellation Hydrus · about 350 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Delicate, petal-like shells surround the galaxy PGC 6240 in this detailed Hubble image, set against a sky crowded with far-off galaxies. PGC 6240 is an elliptical galaxy, a smooth, rounded collection of stars, lying about 350 million light-years away in the southern constellation Hydrus, the Water Snake.
The galaxy is orbited by a number of globular clusters, dense balls of stars, and they contain a mix of young and old stars. That is unusual, since globular clusters are typically made of old stars.

Astronomers think the mixture comes from a galaxy merger that happened fairly recently. In that case, the young clusters are a record of the encounter, a sign that this elliptical galaxy has not always led a quiet life.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.87 x 2.90 arcminutes) and distance (350 million light years), the frame spans roughly 292,000 × 295,000 light-years. Its light set out about 350 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using a blue filter and a near-infrared filter. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The faint shells would be invisible to the eye. Only long exposures reveal them, and part of the data is near-infrared light we cannot see.
